transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, thanks. Um… I guess what finally made me make the appointment is that I’ve been making these, like, technical mistakes at work that I really should know better than to make. I’m a camera operator and editor, so details matter, and lately I’ll do things like label camera cards wrong, miss a timecode note, or export a client cut with the wrong lower-third… even after I thought I checked it.

It sounds small when I say it out loud, and I don’t want to make it seem like I’m careless, because I do care a lot. But it’s been happening enough that it kind of scared me, if that makes sense.
How has your sleep been lately—are you having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling rested when you wake up?

Um… I think it’s mostly okay? I mean, I haven’t really been tracking it closely. I don’t want to overstate it. Some mornings I feel like I could’ve used more sleep, but I don’t know if that’s unusual or just… normal life stuff. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern with falling asleep or waking up a lot, at least not enough that I came in thinking about it.
Have you noticed these kinds of attention or focus problems since childhood or adolescence, or is this something that's really only started recently?

I mean… I think it goes back pretty far, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound like I was a “problem kid” or anything, but even in elementary school my teachers would move my desk around because I was up out of my seat a lot, or I’d blurt out answers, or I’d end up distracting other kids before I really realized I was doing it.

So… yeah, I guess it’s not totally new. I just maybe didn’t think of it that way until now.
Lately, have you noticed yourself feeling persistently worried or on edge about work or other things, even when there's no clear reason to be?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in a constant way, at least. I mean, I do get concerned when I’ve messed something up at work, obviously, but it usually feels tied to an actual thing that happened.

I wouldn’t say I’m just walking around worried for no reason. At least, I haven’t really noticed that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Outside of work, do you notice similar issues—like losing track of things, trouble focusing, or feeling restless—in other areas of your life, such as at home or in social situations?

I’m not totally sure, honestly. I mean… I guess at home I can be a little scattered sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s more than anyone else. Socially, I haven’t really thought of it as a problem.

I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. I notice little things here and there, but I’m not sure I’d say it’s the same level or anything. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Can you give me a specific example of a time at home—like paying bills, doing chores, or keeping track of personal things—where being scattered or losing focus actually caused a problem?

I’m trying to think of a clear example… I don’t know that I have a really good one. I mean, I’ve probably misplaced things or left chores half-done, but nothing is jumping out as a major problem, if that makes sense.

I don’t want to overstate it. At home it feels more like little annoyances than something that’s caused a big consequence. Is that helpful, or are you looking for something more specific?
Do people who know you well—like friends or family—ever comment that you interrupt conversations, have trouble sitting still, or seem restless in social situations?

Yeah… I mean, not constantly, I don’t think. But people have mentioned that I jump in a little quickly sometimes.

At work especially, I’ll catch myself cutting into a conversation, or like… leaning over an assistant’s shoulder to fix something on their timeline before they’ve even asked me to. I’m usually trying to help, but I know it can come across like I don’t trust them, which I feel bad about.

Friends or family might say I interrupt sometimes, but I don’t think they’d say it in a harsh way. Or at least I hope not. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often find yourself finishing other people's sentences, jumping in before they're done talking, or having a hard time waiting your turn—like in lines or during meetings?

Yeah… I think that does happen. I don’t love admitting it, but I’ll sometimes jump in with an answer before the director or a client has even finished asking the question.

It’s usually not meant to be rude — I’m trying to be quick or helpful — but then halfway through my answer I realize I reacted to the first few words and I’m actually answering the wrong thing. Then I have to sort of back up and say, “Sorry, what were you asking?” which is embarrassing.

So yes, I guess I do have a hard time waiting for the full question sometimes. Does that make sense?
Do you often feel physically restless or fidgety—like needing to get up, tap your foot, or feel like you can't sit still for long periods, even outside of work?

Yeah… I think so. I wouldn’t say I’m like pacing around all the time or anything, but sitting still can feel really uncomfortable.

Like during a client screening, when I’m supposed to just sit there and watch quietly, I can feel this kind of pressure building under my skin. Not pain, just this strong urge to get up or do something with my body. I try to keep it contained because I know I’m supposed to be professional, but inside I’m kind of fighting it.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of restlessness you mean, but yes, I do notice it.
Have you ever had distinct periods lasting several days where you felt unusually elevated, euphoric, or needed much less sleep than usual, along with being more impulsive or talkative than normal?

Um… no, I don’t think so. Not in a way that lasted several days or felt like a whole different state.

I mean, I can get really energized if there’s a deadline or a shoot going well, and I might talk more or stay up later, but I wouldn’t say euphoric or like I didn’t need sleep. If I don’t sleep, I usually feel it.

So… I don’t think I’ve had that kind of period, unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean.
